$comment: Capabilities, each admitted by an artefact that already exists in this content model. NO self-assessment: there is no level, no percentage, no proficiency and no years-of-experience field, and _scripts/check-content.mjs fails the build if one appears. A bar chart of skills is a claim about a person; a link to a shipped artefact is evidence, and this system has already decided which of those it prints.
selectionRule: A capability is admitted only if at least one artefact already in projects.json, publications.json, contributions.json or software-archive.json demonstrates it. A human decides inclusion, not a number.
sinceRule: DERIVED, never stated. The year shown is the earliest dated evidence for that capability. An author-supplied 'since' would be a number without a source, which is the one thing content/model.md forbids everywhere else.

capabilities.name: Spectral fitting and peak deconvolution
capabilities.claim: Separating overlapping features in a measured spectrum into components a chemist can argue about, with the fit itself reproducible.

capabilities.name: Ligand-field and term-symbol analysis
capabilities.claim: Turning d-d excitation energies into a ligand-field parameter set, and the diagrams that make the assignment checkable.

capabilities.name: X-ray spectroscopy of transition-metal complexes
capabilities.claim: Reading oxidation state and electronic structure out of RIXS and X-ray emission data, including where the conventional reading fails.

capabilities.name: Model Context Protocol server design
capabilities.claim: Exposing a scientific instrument to a language model as a tool it can call, rather than as prose it has to imitate.

capabilities.name: Packaging and distributing MCP servers
capabilities.claim: Getting a server from a working repository to something a stranger can install without reading the source.

capabilities.name: Static analysis as an agent-callable tool
capabilities.claim: Wrapping linters and type checkers so a model gets a verdict with locations instead of an opinion.

capabilities.name: Release engineering and repository policy
capabilities.claim: Versioning, changelogs and branch policy enforced by a tool rather than by remembering.

capabilities.name: Making software citable
capabilities.claim: Archived releases with concept DOIs, so a method section can point at the exact code that produced a figure.

capabilities.name: Optimisation and numerical methods
capabilities.claim: Implementing and comparing optimisers where the objective is a physical model, not a benchmark function.

capabilities.name: Plotting where the data already is
capabilities.claim: Charts in the terminal and inside the editor, so looking at a column of numbers does not require leaving the tool holding them.

capabilities.name: Colour systems for reading code
capabilities.claim: Editor themes built as a measured palette rather than a set of preferences, including the contrast the palette has to hold.
